problem: Which of the following is the graph of the function $y=-{(\frac{2}{3})}^{x-1}?$
worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y={(\frac{2}{3})}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/fbbddeb527a9ea78b274fd7c4afe9809546a61ba833a67a385cb18aac9e14942.png)

 

- Horizontally shift it by $1$ unit to the right to give $y={(\frac{2}{3})}^{x-1}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(1,1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/617dbba0d17c30ce03da929550d17062fd644ed7992a07b55caa02e5815e7232.png)

- Then, reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-{(\frac{2}{3})}^{x-1}.$ The point $(1,1)$ moves to $(1,-1)$ and the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/7e4d38e401c4ce01330d6082dadd43e50974a55b666023d8b8d51bbcbc7f7258.png)
